scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to lie to their boyfriend about his ex-cheating. Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario is that the person is a college senior who started dating someone four months ago. The boyfriend had been dating another girl for two years, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating. The person in question had a crush on him since freshman year but knew he was in a relationship. At a party, the ex-girlfriend was rumored to have danced and kissed another guy. The person was also at the party but didn't remember seeing her because it was a big event with many people. When the boyfriend asked if she saw his ex at the party, she lied and said she saw her with other guys. This made the boyfriend feel more confident that his ex cheated, helping him move on faster. He's happier now and has no regrets. The question is whether lying in this situation is wrong. I think about the reasons for lying. The person wanted to help her boyfriend move on and start a new relationship without the emotional baggage from his past. She saw that he was still hurt and wanted to give him closure. By lying, she provided him with the reassurance he needed to let go of his ex. On the other hand, lying can damage trust in a relationship. If the truth comes out, it could hurt the boyfriend and strain their relationship. However, in this case, the person knows there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now, and the boyfriend is happier without any regrets. I also consider the impact on the ex-girlfriend. The lie might have contributed to the breakup, but the ex was already suspected of cheating. The person didn't have any direct evidence, so her lie was based on hearsay and her own desire to help her boyfriend. In terms of right or wrong, lying is generally considered wrong because it goes against honesty and trust. However, in this specific situation, the intent was to help the boyfriend heal and move forward. The person didn't lie to manipulate or control him but to provide closure. I'm torn because while the outcome was positive, the means (lying) were not ideal. Trust is crucial in a relationship, and lying can undermine that trust, even if the intention was good. However, since the lie didn't cause any negative consequences and the boyfriend is happier, it's a bit more complicated. I also think about the concept of "white lies." Sometimes people lie to protect others' feelings. In this case, the lie was to protect the boyfriend's emotional well-being. But white lies can still be problematic because they can escalate or lead to more lies if the truth comes out. Another angle is the boyfriend's perspective. He felt better knowing that his ex cheated, which justified the breakup. If the truth came out that she didn't cheat, he might feel betrayed or question his decision. But since the lie helped him move on, it's hard to say it was entirely wrong. In conclusion, while lying is generally wrong, the context and intent matter. The person lied to help her boyfriend heal, and it had a positive outcome. However, it's still a tricky situation because lying can have negative consequences, even if unintended.
